children: Nomura expects a sharp recovery in second-quarter earnings for oil marketing companies (OMCs) despite crude oil prices breaching $100 a barrel, and maintains 'Buy' ratings on Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL). It has a 'Neutral' rating on Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL), which it expects to report a loss in the quarter.

"Despite headline crude oil prices breaching the psychological mark of USD100/bbl recently, we estimate healthy earnings recovery for oil marketing companies (OMCs) given lower average crude oil price in the quarter, a full quarter impact of petrol/diesel price hikes taken in May, and lower LPG underrecovery q-q," Nomura said in its September 11 note.

The brokerage estimates integrated margins for OMCs at $6-12 a barrel in the second quarter, assuming Brent at $107 a barrel for the remainder of the quarter. It expects IOCL and BPCL to report PBT of Rs 32 billion and Rs 26 billion, respectively, while HPCL may report a loss of Rs 28 billion.
"We prefer IOCL and BPCL given their higher exposure towards refining, while HPCL may continue to face challenges from higher oil price due to its higher marketing leverage," Nomura said.

The brokerage also expects gas marketing businesses to benefit from elevated LNG prices. With JKM LNG at around $25/mmbtu, almost double pre-war levels, it expects increased volatility in LNG prices to positively impact the gas marketing businesses of GAIL and Gujarat Energy, both rated 'Buy'.

Nomura expects LNG regasification company Petronet LNG to see further improvement in volumes in the second quarter as offtakers diversify sourcing away from the Middle East. It said PLNG's fixed regas tariff means it "does not face any margin risk", making its business model stable during periods of volatility.

City gas distributors, however, could face margin pressure from higher gas costs, falling domestic gas allocation and limited pass-through. Nomura sees Indraprastha Gas (IGL), rated 'Neutral', as relatively better placed on a sequential margin basis due to its gas sourcing mix, higher CNG price hikes and a lower first-quarter base. It retains a 'Buy' on Mahanagar Gas (MGL), citing strong volume growth potential and scope to raise CNG prices.

On oil prices, Nomura said the prolonged Iran conflict could keep crude prices higher for longer. "We think that the prospect of the war dragging longer than earlier expected may materially impact IEA's oil surplus forecast for 2027, and oil price may remain higher for longer in the near to medium term."

The brokerage also flagged risks to oil flows from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and said Middle East oil flows are down around 40% from pre-war levels. At the same time, a resurgence in Chinese crude demand is putting "upside pressure on oil".

title: Nomura sees sharp Q2 recovery for OMCs despite $100 oil; prefers IOCL, BPCL
